assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening a new observational window: the 2013 detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos beyond atmospheric backgrounds, followed by the 2017 TXS 0506+056 association and the 2023 Galactic-plane evidence, is a genuine discovery enabled by an instrument concept (a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov array in Antarctic ice) that was realised against much scepticism. Importance, originality and lasting impact are all high.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is widely regarded as the scientific driver and principal investigator of IceCube and its AMANDA precursor; Spiering is strongly associated with the long development of neutrino astronomy and the DUMAND/Baikal/AMANDA lineage. A two-person configuration is workable, though the IceCube Collaboration is large and the Baikal and ANTARES/KM3NeT communities and early DUMAND pioneers also have claims.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established and independently supported by multiple analysis channels. The source identification is still thin, with one flaring blazar at about 3 sigma and Galactic-plane evidence, but the discovery of astrophysical neutrinos itself is mature and timely.
uncertainties: I have professional ties to the astroparticle community and use detectors of a related kind, so I discount my own enthusiasm.
I have not verified the exact historical credit division between Halzen, Spiering and the early DUMAND and Baikal leaders.
Source-population identification remains incomplete, so the dominant sources of the diffuse flux are not established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on the magic-wavelength concept, removes the trade-off between atom number and motional systematics and has delivered fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It is a clear invention with direct consequences for precision tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy, and a possible redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock, and Ye's group drove the strontium implementation to record accuracy and stability, including the many-body and spin-squeezing extensions. This is a clean two-person attribution. Ion-clock pioneers such as Wineland and Hänsch were already recognised in earlier prizes, and the Sr-lattice work of Lemonde, Gill and others is unresolved at the margin.
assessment.maturity: Many independent labs have reproduced and surpassed the performance, and international comparisons are routine. Recognition is timely, and the redefinition of the second, expected later this decade, would add to the case.
uncertainties: The relative weight of contributions from Lemonde, Gill, Takamoto and others in the early lattice-clock demonstrations is not settled in my knowledge.
It is unclear whether the committee views this as a sufficiently distinct step from the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, with the prompt experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, opened a very large field of topological quantum matter. It is original, conceptually clean and has lasting influence across condensed matter, photonics and materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 classification and the spin-Hall proposal in graphene. Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive experimental observation, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Koenig et al. Zhang's death and the credit of Bernevig, Hughes, Fu and Moore, and of the 3D materials experimentalists, complicate any three-person set.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many materials and probes for roughly 15 to 20 years, with the 2016 prize covering the earlier topological-phase concepts. Recognition is mature, and the principal risk is overlap with that prior prize.
uncertainties: The attribution among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Fu, Moore and the experimentalists is contested, and the prize cannot include all of them.
Whether the committee regards this as sufficiently beyond the 2016 Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light underpins quantum-enhanced measurement, culminating in its routine use in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600 to beat shot noise in gravitational-wave detection. The combination of a fundamental quantum-optics idea and a decisive application to one of the great instruments of modern physics gives it strong significance and a clear impact.
assessment.attribution: Caves proposed squeezing for interferometry in 1981; Kimble and the Slusher group produced the first experimental squeezed states in the 1980s; Schnabel's group demonstrated and engineered squeezed-light injection in GEO600 and beyond. Mavalvala, the Walls and Lam groups, Slusher and McKenzie also have credible claims, so the configuration is very uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is deployed operationally in the gravitational-wave network, an independent and demanding confirmation. The idea and application are mature, but the credit allocation is the main unresolved issue.
uncertainties: Missing from the supplied credit are Slusher and others who made the first squeezed-state measurements, so the prize configuration is only approximate.
The 2017 prize already recognised LIGO, which could reduce enthusiasm for a closely linked topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire-materials field in a few years. It combines an elegant theoretical insight with a surprising experimental discovery.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery together with Cao and others. The configuration is natural, although Cory Dean, Kim and others, and Cao as the lead author, are unresolved, as are Yacoby and other contemporaries.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups and extended to other moire systems, but the underlying mechanism of the superconductivity is still under debate. Recognition within a few years would be fast, though not unprecedented.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and the overall interpretation of the correlated phases remain unsettled.
Credit for the early graphene-twist experiments and for the student leading the 2018 work could be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* provide direct visual evidence of black-hole shadows and test strong-field gravity. As a feat of instrumentation (a planet-scale VLBI array at 1.3 mm with calibration and imaging innovations) it is very impressive and has wide public and scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow-imaging idea in 1999, and Doeleman led the mm-VLBI technical development and the EHT collaboration. Zensus and others were instrumental to the organisation. The result is also a collaboration of hundreds, and individual attribution is very hard to defend.
assessment.maturity: Two sources imaged and the results consistent with general relativity, but the physics extracted (spin, jet launching, alternatives to GR) is still limited and subject to modelling systematics. Recognition may be somewhat early relative to the follow-up science.
uncertainties: The fair attribution within a very large collaboration and between the idea, instrument and imaging-algorithm contributions is unclear.
Precision tests of gravity from the images remain model dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP's all-sky maps determined the key parameters of the standard cosmological model to percent-level precision and established the age, geometry and composition of the Universe. It is a landmark of precision cosmology and a high-quality, well-engineered experiment with enduring impact.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was central to the instrument and design heritage, and Spergel led the interpretation and parameter analysis. The credit overlaps with the COBE prize of 2006 and the 2019 prize for physical cosmology, and with the Planck team's role, so the configuration is conceivable but not obviously decisive.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and superseded by Planck, with consistent parameters over two decades. It is mature, and the open question is whether more recognition is appropriate given the earlier prizes in the area.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees WMAP as a distinct enough step beyond COBE and the 2019 cosmology prize.
The roles of Wilkinson, Wright, Hinshaw and others in WMAP are not captured in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors made precision vertexing and tracking possible at colliders and later in medical and X-ray imaging, and they underlie discoveries at the LHC. The work is a clear instrument-driven enabling technology, in the tradition of the Charpak prize, with considerable lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Parker developed the 3D and microstrip detectors, Heijne pioneered the silicon strip and pixel concepts at CERN, and Campbell led the Medipix and hybrid pixel developments. Other people, such as Kemmer, Hallewell and Rossi, and large teams contributed, which makes a three-person prize debatable.
assessment.maturity: Used for decades in all major collider experiments and in photon-counting imaging, so well confirmed through use. The case is mature, and the question is mainly the attribution among many contributors.
uncertainties: I work in detector instrumentation myself, so I may over-value this area, and I have not verified the detailed credit among Heijne, Campbell, Parker and Kemmer.
It is unclear if the committee wishes to honour detector technology so soon after other instrument-related awards.
